findings.subject: observationalconditions.obsdate
findings.statement: Data covers 2015-02-23 to 2025-02-09, spanning 121 distinct month(s). Anything outside that window is absent rather than zero, and a trend that ends at 2025-02-09 is an artefact of the extract, not a real decline.

evidence.sql: SELECT CAST(MIN(try_strptime("obsdate", '%Y-%m-%d')) AS DATE), CAST(MAX(try_strptime("obsdate", '%Y-%m-%d')) AS DATE), COUNT(DISTINCT date_trunc('month', try_strptime("obsdate", '%Y-%m-%d'))) FROM "observationalconditions"

findings.subject: observationalconditions.signalref
findings.statement: signalref joins to signals.signalregistry for 100.0% of the 1,000 rows that populate it. The relationship is many-to-one, so a join will not fan out and sums stay correct.

evidence.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS referencing,
                   ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN m."signalregistry" IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                         / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_matched,
                   (SELECT COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT "signalregistry") FROM "signals")
                     AS peer_key_unique
            FROM "observationalconditions" c
            LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT "signalregistry" FROM "signals") m
              ON c."signalref" = m."signalregistry"
            WHERE c."signalref" IS NOT NULL AND c."signalref" <> ''

findings.subject: technicalinfo.techmsgref
findings.statement: techmsgref joins to messaginganalysis.msgkey for 100.0% of the 998 rows that populate it. The relationship is many-to-one, so a join will not fan out and sums stay correct.

evidence.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS referencing,
                   ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN m."msgkey" IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                         / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_matched,
                   (SELECT COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT "msgkey") FROM "messaginganalysis")
                     AS peer_key_unique
            FROM "technicalinfo" c
            LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT "msgkey" FROM "messaginganalysis") m
              ON c."techmsgref" = m."msgkey"
            WHERE c."techmsgref" IS NOT NULL AND c."techmsgref" <> ''

findings.subject: location.latitude
findings.statement: Values fall into 2 distinct format classes. The dominant class is numeric (example 60.155064, 512 rows); 488 rows use a different format, for example: -60.008683. The column therefore holds more than one kind of identifier, and filtering as if it held one will silently drop rows.

evidence.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_matches("latitude", '^[0-9.]+$') THEN 'numeric' WHEN regexp_matches("latitude", '[0-9]') THEN 'alphanumeric' WHEN regexp_matches("latitude", '^[A-Za-z]+$') THEN 'word' ELSE 'phrase' END AS shape, COUNT(*) AS rows, MIN("latitude") AS example FROM "location" WHERE "latitude" IS NOT NULL AND "latitude" <> '' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1

findings.subject: location.loceqref
findings.statement: loceqref joins to equipment.equipmentcode for 100.0% of the 1,000 rows that populate it. The relationship is many-to-one, so a join will not fan out and sums stay correct.

evidence.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS referencing,
                   ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN m."equipmentcode" IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
                         / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_matched,
                   (SELECT COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT "equipmentcode") FROM "equipment")
                     AS peer_key_unique
            FROM "location" c
            LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT "equipmentcode" FROM "equipment") m
              ON c."loceqref" = m."equipmentcode"
            WHERE c."loceqref" IS NOT NULL AND c."loceqref" <> ''

findings.statement: Values fall into 2 distinct format classes. The dominant class is phrase (example AI Generated, 477 rows); 462 rows use a different format, for example: 2D. The column therefore holds more than one kind of identifier, and filtering as if it held one will silently drop rows.

evidence.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN regexp_matches("kindtag", '^[0-9.]+$') THEN 'numeric' WHEN regexp_matches("kindtag", '[0-9]') THEN 'alphanumeric' WHEN regexp_matches("kindtag", '^[A-Za-z]+$') THEN 'word' ELSE 'phrase' END AS shape, COUNT(*) AS rows, MIN("kindtag") AS example FROM "virtualidols" WHERE "kindtag" IS NOT NULL AND "kindtag" <> '' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1

findings.subject: virtualidols.assocgroup
findings.statement: 53 value families have more than one variant spelling: Smith (8 variants), Brown (7 variants), Nelson (5 variants), Harris (4 variants), Lee (4 variants), Simmons (4 variants), Chavez (3 variants), Jackson (3 variants) .... Grouping on the raw value splits each family into separate categories.

evidence.sql:
SELECT stem, COUNT(*) AS variants FROM (
              SELECT DISTINCT CASE WHEN strpos("assocgroup", ',') > 0 THEN trim(split_part("assocgroup", ',', 1)) ELSE trim("assocgroup") END AS stem, "assocgroup" AS full_value
              FROM "virtualidols" WHERE "assocgroup" IS NOT NULL AND "assocgroup" <> ''
            ) GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
            ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1

findings.subject: virtualidols.genretag
findings.statement: Holds 5 distinct values: Electronic (196), Pop (195), Traditional (194), Rock (180), Dance (174).

evidence.sql: SELECT "genretag", COUNT(*) FROM "virtualidols" GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 1
